lessonTitle: Nucleus, Ribosomes and the Endomembrane System

blocks.text: In a pancreatic acinar cell the basal cytoplasm stains deep blue with haematoxylin, and the apex is packed with pink granules; in an adrenal cortical cell the cytoplasm is pale and foamy. The two cells run different cellular factories, and the nucleus, ribosomes and endoplasmic reticulum explain why.

blocks.markdown: The **nucleus** holds the genome and directs protein synthesis. Its **nuclear envelope** is two membranes (inner and outer) separated by a perinuclear space; the outer membrane is continuous with the rough endoplasmic reticulum (rER). **Nuclear pore complexes** perforate the envelope and control traffic: small molecules diffuse, whereas proteins carrying a **nuclear localisation signal** are bound by **importins** and actively transported in, and RNAs and ribosomal subunits are exported. The **nuclear lamina**, a meshwork of lamin filaments under the inner membrane, supports the envelope. Chromatin is **euchromatin** (loosely packed, pale, transcriptionally active) or **heterochromatin** (condensed, dark, inactive).

blocks.title: Nucleolus and ribosomes
blocks.text: The nucleolus is a dense region, not membrane-bound, where ribosomal RNA genes are transcribed and ribosomal subunits are assembled from rRNA and imported ribosomal proteins. A ribosome is a complex of rRNA and protein that translates mRNA, made of a large (60S) and a small (40S) subunit that together form the 80S eukaryotic ribosome. Cells that make a lot of protein have a prominent nucleolus.

blocks.markdown: **Free and bound ribosomes.** Ribosomes translating cytosolic, nuclear, mitochondrial and peroxisomal proteins are free in the cytosol. A ribosome making a secretory, membrane or lysosomal protein is directed to the rER because the nascent chain begins with a **signal peptide**. The **signal recognition particle (SRP)** binds the signal peptide, pauses translation and docks the ribosome on a translocon in the rER membrane. The chain is threaded into the lumen, the signal peptide is cleaved, and the protein is folded with chaperones and given N-linked sugars.

rows: Studded with ribosomes; abundant in plasma cells and acinar cells (basophilic cytoplasm)
Synthesis, folding and glycosylation of secretory, membrane and lysosomal proteins
Tubular network without ribosomes; extensive in steroid-secreting cells and hepatocytes; in muscle called sarcoplasmic reticulum
Steroid and lipid synthesis, detoxification by cytochrome P450 enzymes, Ca2+ storage
Stack of cisternae with cis (receiving) and trans (shipping) faces
Modifies glycoproteins, sorts cargo (e.g. mannose-6-phosphate tags lysosomal enzymes), packages vesicles
Membrane-bound granules budding from the trans-Golgi
Store product and release by exocytosis

blocks.title: Tracing a secreted protein
blocks.prompt: Insulin precursor is synthesised in a pancreatic beta cell. Trace its route to the cell surface.

steps.text: The ribosome begins translation in the cytosol; the signal peptide is recognised by SRP and the ribosome docks on the rER translocon.
The chain enters the rER lumen, the signal peptide is removed and the protein folds and is glycosylated or modified.
Transport vesicles carry it to the cis Golgi; it moves through the stack and is modified and sorted at the trans-Golgi.
It is packaged into secretory vesicles that fuse with the plasma membrane in response to a stimulus (exocytosis).

blocks.answer: Free ribosome, SRP, rER, vesicle, cis to trans Golgi, secretory vesicle, exocytosis.

blocks.title: Rough or smooth ER?
blocks.prompt: A hepatocyte is exposed to phenobarbital for days and its smooth ER expands. Another cell synthesises steroids. Which ER carries out each function, and how does the drug-metabolising enzyme get there?

steps.text: Cytochrome P450 enzymes are made on rough ER ribosomes like other membrane proteins, then reside in the smooth ER membrane where they metabolise drugs and toxins.
Repeated exposure induces more enzyme and more smooth ER membrane, so the smooth ER hypertrophies.
Steroid hormones are synthesised in the smooth ER of steroid-secreting cells such as adrenal cortex cells.

blocks.answer: Smooth ER for both drug metabolism and steroid synthesis, although the P450 proteins are first made on rough ER.

items: Nuclear envelope: double membrane continuous with rER, with pores; nucleolus makes rRNA and assembles ribosomal subunits.
Secretory protein route: signal peptide, SRP, rER, vesicle, Golgi cis to trans, secretory vesicle, exocytosis.
rER makes secretory proteins; sER makes steroids and lipids and detoxifies drugs.

blocks.title: Common exam trap
blocks.text: A protein is not sent to the rER by the ribosome type but by its own signal peptide: ribosomes are identical, and only those translating a signal-peptide-bearing chain dock on the rER.

points: The nuclear envelope is a double membrane with pores, continuous with the rER; the nucleolus makes rRNA and assembles ribosomal subunits.
Secretory proteins are targeted by a signal peptide and SRP to the rER, then pass through the Golgi and secretory vesicles to the cell surface.
The rER synthesises and processes proteins; the sER synthesises steroids and lipids, stores calcium and detoxifies drugs.

questions.stem: Which description of the nuclear envelope is correct?

options.text: Two membranes with pores, the outer being continuous with the rough ER
A single membrane without pores, separate from the ER
Two membranes with no connection to the ER, sealed except at the nucleolus
A single membrane continuous with the Golgi apparatus

questions.correctOptionText: Two membranes with pores, the outer being continuous with the rough ER

distractorRationale.b: It is a double membrane with pores.
distractorRationale.c: It is continuous with the ER and has pores throughout.
distractorRationale.d: Its outer membrane is continuous with the rER, not the Golgi.

questions.explanation: The envelope is a double membrane whose outer layer is continuous with the rER, and nuclear pore complexes control transport. A nuclear lamina supports its inner face.

questions.stem: A section of a rapidly growing tumour shows cells with very prominent, large nucleoli. What does this suggest?

options.text: High rates of ribosomal RNA synthesis and ribosome assembly to support protein production
Abundant smooth ER for drug detoxification
Loss of the nuclear envelope
Storage of steroid hormones in the nucleolus

questions.correctOptionText: High rates of ribosomal RNA synthesis and ribosome assembly to support protein production

distractorRationale.b: That is not a nucleolar function.
distractorRationale.c: The envelope is not lost in interphase.
distractorRationale.d: Steroids are made in the smooth ER.

questions.explanation: The nucleolus is the site of rRNA transcription and ribosomal subunit assembly. Cells that grow and synthesise a lot of protein need many ribosomes and so show prominent nucleoli.

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly describes the route of a secreted protein after synthesis begins?

options.text: Rough ER, transport vesicle, cis Golgi, trans Golgi, secretory vesicle, exocytosis
Trans Golgi, cis Golgi, rough ER, lysosome, exocytosis
Smooth ER, nucleus, secretory vesicle, plasma membrane
Rough ER, lysosome, trans Golgi, mitochondrion

questions.correctOptionText: Rough ER, transport vesicle, cis Golgi, trans Golgi, secretory vesicle, exocytosis

distractorRationale.c: Secretory proteins do not pass through the nucleus.
distractorRationale.d: Secreted proteins are not routed through lysosomes or mitochondria.

questions.explanation: Secretory proteins enter the rER, are carried in vesicles to the cis Golgi, move to the trans Golgi, are packaged into secretory vesicles and are released by exocytosis.

questions.stem: A mutation deletes the signal peptide of a hormone precursor. Where is the protein most likely to end up?

options.text: Synthesised on free ribosomes and retained in the cytosol, not secreted
Synthesised on the rough ER and secreted normally
Imported into the nucleolus
Delivered to the smooth ER for steroid synthesis

questions.correctOptionText: Synthesised on free ribosomes and retained in the cytosol, not secreted

distractorRationale.b: Without a signal peptide, SRP does not target the ribosome to the rER.
distractorRationale.c: Nucleolar import needs a nuclear localisation signal.
distractorRationale.d: Smooth ER is not the route for protein secretion.

questions.explanation: The signal peptide is recognised by the SRP, which brings the ribosome to the rER. Without it, translation continues on free ribosomes and the protein stays in the cytosol.

questions.stem: A patient takes a drug for months and a liver biopsy shows hepatocytes with greatly expanded tubular membrane networks lacking ribosomes. Which organelle has expanded and why?

options.text: Smooth ER, because induced drug-metabolising enzymes need more membrane
Rough ER, because more secretory proteins are made
Golgi apparatus, because more lysosomes are formed
Nucleolus, because more rRNA is made

questions.correctOptionText: Smooth ER, because induced drug-metabolising enzymes need more membrane

distractorRationale.c: The expanded membranes are ER-like tubules.
distractorRationale.d: The nucleolus is not a membrane network.

questions.explanation: Cytochrome P450 enzymes of the smooth ER are induced by repeated drug exposure, and the smooth ER proliferates to accommodate them. Hypertrophy of smooth ER is therefore an adaptive response.

questions.stem: Electron micrographs of two cells show (X) a basal cytoplasm filled with stacked ribosome-studded cisternae and (Y) a cytoplasm full of branching tubules without ribosomes and lipid droplets. Which pairing is most plausible?

options.text: X is an antibody-secreting plasma cell and Y is a steroid-secreting adrenal cortical cell
X is a steroid-secreting cell and Y is a plasma cell
Both are plasma cells
X is a mature erythrocyte and Y is a neurone

questions.correctOptionText: X is an antibody-secreting plasma cell and Y is a steroid-secreting adrenal cortical cell

distractorRationale.d: A mature erythrocyte has no organelles.

questions.explanation: Abundant rough ER marks cells exporting protein such as plasma cells, whereas abundant smooth ER and lipid droplets mark steroid-synthesising cells.

questions.stem: Describe the structure of the nuclear envelope and the function of the nucleolus.
markingGuide: Double membrane (inner and outer) with a perinuclear space.
Outer membrane continuous with the rough ER.
Nuclear pore complexes control transport of proteins and RNAs.
Nucleolus: transcription of rRNA and assembly of ribosomal subunits.
questions.explanation: A strong answer includes the double membrane and pores as well as the nucleolus's role in ribosome biogenesis.

questions.stem: Trace a secreted glycoprotein from the start of translation to its release at the cell surface, naming the signals and compartments involved.
markingGuide: Translation starts on a free ribosome; the signal peptide is recognised by SRP.
The ribosome docks on a translocon and the chain enters the rER lumen; signal peptide is cleaved.
Folding and N-glycosylation in the rER.
Vesicle transport to the cis Golgi, passage to the trans Golgi with modification and sorting.
Packaging in secretory vesicles and release by exocytosis.
questions.explanation: The pathway is defined by the signal peptide and then successive compartments. A full answer names each step in order.

questions.stem: Distinguish the roles of the rough and smooth endoplasmic reticulum, giving a cell type in which each predominates.
markingGuide: Rough ER has ribosomes and makes secretory, membrane and lysosomal proteins; e.g. plasma cell or pancreatic acinar cell.
Smooth ER lacks ribosomes and synthesises lipids and steroids, detoxifies drugs, stores calcium.
Example of smooth ER predominance: steroid-secreting cell or hepatocyte (also sarcoplasmic reticulum in muscle).
questions.explanation: The ribosome studding defines rough ER and its protein role, whereas smooth ER handles lipid metabolism and detoxification.

questions.stem: A newly made transcription factor must enter the nucleus. Which statement best describes how it does so?

options.text: A nuclear localisation signal is bound by importin and the complex is actively transported through a nuclear pore
It diffuses passively through the lipid bilayer of the envelope
It is carried in a vesicle that fuses with the outer nuclear membrane
It enters through the rough ER lumen via the signal peptide

questions.correctOptionText: A nuclear localisation signal is bound by importin and the complex is actively transported through a nuclear pore

distractorRationale.b: Large proteins cannot cross the bilayer.
distractorRationale.c: Nuclear import does not use vesicle fusion.

questions.explanation: Nuclear proteins carry a localisation signal bound by importins, which ferry them through pores in an energy-dependent process. This is distinct from the signal-peptide route to the rER.

questions.stem: A lysosomal enzyme is made on the rER. In which compartment is it tagged with mannose-6-phosphate for delivery to lysosomes?

options.text: The Golgi apparatus
The nucleolus
The cytosol
The smooth ER of a steroid cell

distractorRationale.d: Smooth ER is not the tagging site.

questions.explanation: Golgi enzymes add mannose-6-phosphate to lysosomal enzymes, and receptors in the trans-Golgi package them into vesicles destined for lysosomes. This is an example of Golgi sorting.
